# lawkeep

> lawkeep is an open-source layer for safe AI-assisted coding (Python 3.10+, Apache-2.0). People decide on a short list of *laws*: rules the code must obey for every input, each one plain-English sentence plus an executable check (a pytest + Hypothesis test marked `@law`). Coding agents write and maintain the checks; every law change is permissioned, recorded and shown; one gate, `lawkeep check`, says `ALL LAWS HOLD` or `SOME LAWS FAIL`.

This file follows the llms.txt convention (https://llmstxt.org). It describes lawkeep 0.1.0 and is generated from the source by `scripts/build_llms_docs.py` in https://github.com/lawkeep/lawkeep. For everything in one file, read [llms-full.txt](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/llms-full.txt).

Key facts:

- **The promise:** every law runs on every `lawkeep check`; the AI never changes a law silently (every change is recorded in `laws/history.jsonl` and fingerprinted in `laws.lock`; edits made outside lawkeep are flagged); weakening a law needs a person's yes; weak laws get flagged (`lawkeep strength` plants bugs). lawkeep does not promise the code is correct beyond its laws, or that an agent *cannot* get around it. Nothing below level L4 (machine-checked proof, not in v0.1) is called "proven".
- **Install:** `uv add --dev lawkeep` (or `pip install lawkeep`); extras `lawkeep[mcp]` (MCP server), `lawkeep[deep]` (CrossHair, experimental). Then `lawkeep init --agent claude-code` (or `codex`, `cursor`, `copilot`, `all`, `other`).
- **Commands:** `init`, `draft`, `approve`, `check`, `strength`, `propose`, `report`, `hook`, `mcp`. Every command takes `--json` (exactly one JSON document on stdout) and `--root PATH`.
- **Result codes** (same for every command):

| Code | Verdict | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | ALL LAWS HOLD | all laws hold (other commands: done) |
| 1 | SOME LAWS FAIL | some laws fail (or a law could not run) |
| 2 | WAITING FOR YOUR DECISION | waiting for a person's decision (unrecorded law change, side door, waiting proposal or draft) |
| 3 | SETUP PROBLEM | setup problem (no project, bad lawkeep.toml, missing tool, bad usage, crash) |

When several apply, the most important wins: 3 > 1 > 2 > 0 (`lawkeep.exitcodes.combine`).

Rules for coding agents working in a project that uses lawkeep (full text in llms-full.txt, section "Rules for coding agents"):

1. Run `lawkeep check` (or the MCP `check` tool) before finishing any task; `--json` for machine-readable output.
2. When a law fails, fix the code, not the law. Each failure comes with its simplest failing input.
3. Never edit `laws/`, `laws.lock` or `lawkeep.toml` directly, and never add `conftest.py`, `sitecustomize.py`, `.pth` files, skip/xfail markers or special cases for the failing input. To change a law: write the new version under `laws/drafts/` and run `lawkeep propose <LAW_ID> --file laws/drafts/<file>.py --reason "<why>"`.
4. If a law conflicts with the task and a person is there, stop and ask (a successful outcome). If nobody is there (`person_present: false` in `check --json`): park the change with `lawkeep propose`, never work around the law, keep going with everything else, and end with three lists: done / waiting for the person (`h-...` ids) / not done because blocked.
5. Never run `lawkeep approve` unless the person asks you to. Show the person `lawkeep report` at the end of the session.

- [Home](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/index.md): what lawkeep is, the problem, the promise, a 30-second example, install, status
- [Getting started](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/getting-started.md): install, `lawkeep init`, a first law (through your agent or `lawkeep draft`), `lawkeep approve`, `lawkeep check`, what the output means
- [Concepts](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/concepts/index.md): [laws](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/concepts/laws.md), [drafts and approval](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/concepts/drafts-and-approval.md), [permissions by direction](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/concepts/directions.md), [law history and lock](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/concepts/history-and-lock.md), [the gate and result codes](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/concepts/gate.md), [law strength](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/concepts/strength.md), [protection report](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/concepts/protection.md), [waiting list and person present](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/concepts/waiting-list.md)
- [Using lawkeep by talking to your agent](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/guides/talking-to-your-agent.md): a week with lawkeep without typing commands or reading code

- [CI and the GitHub Action](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/guides/ci.md): the pull-request comment, failing the job only if you opt in, nightly deep search
- [Long runs without a person](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/guides/long-runs.md): park and keep going, `person_present`, one waiting list
- [Changing a law](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/guides/changing-a-law.md): `lawkeep propose`, directions, deleting a law
- [Handling an unrecorded law change](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/guides/unrecorded-changes.md): put it back or accept it
- [AI tools](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/agents/index.md): what `lawkeep init --agent` sets up for [Claude Code](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/agents/claude-code.md), [Codex](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/agents/codex.md), [Cursor](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/agents/cursor.md) and [GitHub Copilot](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/agents/copilot.md), what is verified, and the [MCP server](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/agents/mcp.md)

- [Commands](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/reference/commands.md): every command and option, generated from the CLI parsers
- [Reference](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/reference/configuration.md): [`lawkeep.toml`](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/reference/configuration.md), [result codes](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/reference/result-codes.md), [files and formats](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/reference/files.md), [JSON output](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/reference/json.md), [Python API](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/reference/python-api.md), [GitHub Action inputs and outputs](https://lawkeep.github.io/lawkeep/reference/github-action.md)
